title: Prefill & Constraint Composer for Batch+Cache Policies — lightweight explainer flow
creator: Maya Singh
description: Design a compact composer that pre-populates batching and KV/prefix-cache constraints using workload telemetry and guided explainers. The feature is targeted at engineers and platform owners who want quick, trustworthy recommendations without deep manual tuning. Goals: reduce time-to-config by 60%, prevent obvious misconfigurations with guardrails, and provide a lightweight simulator that shows estimated latency and cost impact before applying policies.
acceptance_criteria: Composer loads suggested settings derived from per-route telemetry (p95 latency, mean tokens, cache hit rate) when a route is opened for policy configuration
Every suggested setting is accompanied by a concise one-line rationale and a link to a deeper explainer panel
Users can apply a suggestion as-is, tweak parameters through simple sliders/inputs, or opt for an advanced mode with full knobs
Preview/dry-run sim shows estimated % change in token cost and expected 95th percentile latency with a confidence band based on recent workload variance

Guardrails prevent selecting combinations that violate SLOs or could cause state explosion (e.g., per-request KV cache size > 50k tokens) and surface an inline warning with recommended corrective action
All composer actions produce audit-log friendly notes (human-readable) saved to the rollout record
Design passes usability test with at least 6 platform engineers with SUS >= 75 and qualitative feedback indicating trust in suggestions
decisions: Use telemetry-derived defaults as the primary affordance; do not hide the source of the recommendation (show metric snippet)
Expose two UX paths: Quick Apply (1-click suggestion) and Tweak (compact sliders + single-line rationale)
Include an optional Advanced view for power users; defaults should be safe for most workloads
Visualize estimates as delta bars with confidence bands, not absolute promises, to set appropriate expectations
Guardrails implemented client-side in the composer UI and enforced server-side at rollout time to avoid drift
tradeoffs: Simplicity vs. control: Quick Apply reduces cognitive load but may hide fine-grained tuning — mitigated by Tweak mode and explicit 'why this' rationale
Telemetry freshness vs. stability: Using very recent metrics gives better tailoring but may cause volatile recommendations; we use a 7-day rolling window by default

Estimation accuracy vs. complexity: The dry-run model will be intentionally conservative to avoid overpromising; advanced users can opt into a higher-fidelity simulation that requires historical trace processing
risks: Users might over-trust 1-click suggestions and apply them across dissimilar routes — mitigate with stronger route-level rationale and a 'compare routes' hint
Incorrect telemetry mapping for custom models could create suboptimal defaults — plan to validate mapping for top 10 customer models first
Edge-case workloads (e.g., bursty short conversations) may need special presets, which are outside v1 scope
research_plan: Conduct 1:1 sessions with 6 platform/ML engineers to validate mental model of 'prefill' vs. 'manual tuning'
Run A/B on rollout adoption: quick-apply enabled vs. control (no suggestions) measuring time-to-first-policy and rollback rate
Collect qualitative feedback on the clarity of rationale and confidence bands
